item.title: Will people skip work and hurt the U.S. economy to play Grand Theft Auto 6?
item.description:
The biggest video game of the decade drops tonight. Grand Theft Auto VI has already made an estimated $1.5 billion in pre-orders and earned glowing reviews, but those who worked tirelessly on it may also make history with a bid for union recognition and to negotiate with their employer over working conditions. The employer is Rockstar Games, one of the largest video game studios in the world, based in New York City and with twelve other offices across the globe. GTA VI is the latest in a series that launched in 1997 and has since sold roughly 480 million copies. “Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar,” Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar, wrote in the Guardian on Wednesday. “What happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the…

item.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' arrives with enormous hype and expectations after 13-year wait
item.description:
'Grand Theft Auto VI' lead Lucia Caminos is a fiercely ambitious woman who sees crime as a means of escaping the circumstances she's been born into. Rockstar Games If the Netflix-exclusive trailer that briefly crashed the streaming service in August 2026 is any indication, “ Grand Theft Auto VI ” – a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style crime saga set in a satirical, fictionalized Florida – may be the most anticipated video game of all time . item.title: Israeli settler kills Palestinian grandmother in occupied West Bank
item.description:
Israeli soldiers who are occupying my home in Turmus Ayya on Nov. 12, 2006. Photo by Zain Jaafar/ AFP via Getty Images Late last month, Israeli soldiers broke down the doors to my family’s home in the occupied West Bank, took over the house, and didn’t leave for almost three weeks. I am a Palestinian American, a U.S. citizen. So are my children. The occupation of my home in Palestine is deeply alarming, and the response I received from my own government here in the United States has been profoundly disappointing. It started on Oct. 25, 2026, when the Israeli military invaded my family’s home in Turmus Ayya, in the northern Ramallah area of the occupied West Bank. item.title: MLB commissioner Manfred cites fan support for salary cap as baseball heads towards lockout
item.description:
This article was written by Jason Foster and published on Sport & State , a new media company founded by Clay Travis that is built around sports, culture, original voices, and live conversation. * * * * * We’re about two weeks from a near-certain MLB lockout , and here’s what we know: The players do not want a salary cap . What we don’t know is what the players do want. As the Dec. 1 expiration of the current collective bargaining agreement approaches, the MLB Players Association has yet to offer any public counter-proposal to a salary cap. It’s just been an immediate and standard Nope. Next. to every salvo from the owners. Meanwhile, the owners have been all about public messaging. In fact, with the full backing of the league’s vast communication resources, they’ve essentially framed their entire proposal for a cap around public opinion polls that show a majority of fans would support…

item.title: Israeli military launches rare ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
item.description:
The Israeli military said it had launched an operation on Wednesday in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, where an AFP journalist saw Israeli tanks position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp. The rare ground operation comes after inconclusive Israeli elections, with the opposition's Gadi Eisenkot trying to form a government without caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel's security. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.
